The model sees a near coin flip tonight, with ANA at 3.02 expected goals and NYI at 3.06 (expected goals measure the quality of chances a team creates). Neither side has controlled play at five on five: ANA has taken 46% of the expected goals in its games and NYI 49%. The Ducks create a bit more (3.22 expected goals for per 60 minutes to 2.74) but allow 3.46, the same as the Islanders. Special teams favor ANA, whose penalty kill allows 0.72 expected goals a game to NYI's 1.14, and NYI takes 4.75 penalties a game. The Ducks are on the second night of a back-to-back after a 2-5 loss at the Rangers, and they are winless in three (0-3-0), outscored 13-6, with 44% of the expected goals in that stretch. The Islanders have two days of rest and are 3-1-1 in their last five despite 46% of the expected goals. Both teams are missing forwards: NYI without Matias Maccelli and Calum Ritchie, ANA without Ryan Poehling.

The goalie matchup leans to the home side. Projected starter Ilya Sorokin is at .940 this season, 8.47 goals saved above expected (how many goals a goalie stops beyond what the shot quality would predict), and .943 with 8.0 over his last five starts. Last season he was at +22.3 over 55 games. Projected ANA starter Lukas Dostal is at +0.7 this year and was at -3.71 over 56 games last season.

Bo Horvat is the player to watch for NYI, with a 41% chance to score and 71% to record a point, flagged as due to cool. For ANA, Beckett Sennecke (32% to score) and Leo Carlsson (69% to record a point) are the likeliest sources of offense.
